cases.lesson_title: Bạn đang giới thiệu Anna với bạn mới. Thay tên riêng sao cho không lặp.
cases.passage_en: A small notice for a family book swap has been placed near the entrance to the town library. The librarian is helping with a family book swap. There is one small problem: some covers are missing. Some people have ideas, but the team needs more time. On Tuesday, the librarian counted 19 picture books at the town library. The notice is on the desk. The group is still thinking about the new plan. It has not said yes. The final review is scheduled for Monday. Visitors can read the instructions before joining. They can ask for help if they do not understand a sign. The team wants the area to be easy to use.

questions.prompt_vi: Bài tập cấu trúc song song từ A1-01 (Bạn đang giới thiệu Anna với bạn mới. Thay tên riêng sao cho không lặp.): Tom and I are students. Chọn đại từ thay Tom and I.
options_en: They
We
Us
rationales_vi: They chỉ nhóm người không bao gồm người nói, còn Tom and I gồm cả người nói. Đây là bài vận dụng song song theo chủ điểm Grammar, không phải câu trích từ đoạn văn.
Có người nói (I) trong nhóm, nên dùng we. Đây là bài vận dụng song song theo chủ điểm Grammar, không phải câu trích từ đoạn văn.
Us là đại từ tân ngữ; ở vị trí chủ ngữ cần We. Đây là bài vận dụng song song theo chủ điểm Grammar, không phải câu trích từ đoạn văn.

There is one small problem: one frame is damaged. Some people have ideas, but the team needs more time. On Wednesday, the art teacher counted 26 paintings at the school hall. There are three signs by the door. The group is still thinking about the new plan. It has not said yes. The final review is scheduled for Friday. The door will open at the usual time. People should keep their personal things with them. A staff member can answer simple questions.

is

Staff have identified a problem that may require a separate response: a section is being resurfaced. Some visitors have asked for changes, but the team has not checked them yet. cases.passage_en: The local team is reviewing an air quality study at the school laboratory after several participants asked for clearer instructions. For an air quality study, the science coordinator is comparing the current plan with the written record. The purpose of this note is to help readers distinguish the event itself from the decisions that may follow. The team has not yet resolved a specific concern: one sensor provided inconsistent readings. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Monday, the science coordinator counted 19 sensor kits at the school laboratory. The coordinator has checked the latest figures, but the result is still provisional. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Wednesday. The record includes a short account of how the information was gathered. Several participants contributed comments, but those comments were not independently verified. The team therefore kept the figures, the suggestions and the proposed action in separate sections of its report. A separate note contains a visitor suggestion, but it has not been independently checked.

Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. People involved in the work have been asked not to circulate an unverified final timetable. On Wednesday, the council assistant counted 33 feedback forms at the park office. One participant recalled a different sequence of events, yet the written log is the only record agreed by the team.

cases.passage_en: The people responsible for a recruitment drive at the charity office are trying to reconcile the timetable with the available resources. To avoid repeating an earlier mistake, the programme lead is preparing an evidence-based note about a recruitment drive. One unresolved practical issue is that some records contain duplicated names. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Tuesday, the programme lead counted 31 volunteer badges at the charity office. By the time visitors arrived, the team had checked the signs. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Saturday. People working on the project have suggested different solutions. Some favour a quicker change, while others argue that the existing evidence is too limited. For now, the written report presents both positions without pretending that agreement has been reached. One participant recalled a different sequence of events, yet the written log is the only record agreed by the team.

Responsibility for the current review of an outreach assessment rests with the programme evaluator, rather than with an outside authority. The purpose of this note is to help readers distinguish the event itself from the decisions that may follow. An important limitation in the current arrangements is that follow-up rates vary by village. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Tuesday, the programme evaluator counted 17 service referrals at the district clinic. The outcome was reported to have been influenced by the schedule. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. Participants who favoured immediate action highlighted accessibility, while others emphasised the limited evidence base. In particular, the team will retain the source of each figure, the date it was recorded and any assumptions used in the comparison. This prevents subsequent readers from confusing a documented observation with an interpretation produced during the meeting. The preliminary record covers only the activity described here and should not be generalised to every site.

cases.passage_en: The internal review of a cycle-lane pilot has produced a provisional recommendation, although the supporting evidence remains uneven. The traffic engineer has been assigned to prepare a clear update on a cycle-lane pilot for the next discussion. A note from the previous meeting records that the observation periods are unequal. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. People involved in the work have been asked not to circulate an unverified final timetable. On Thursday, the traffic engineer counted 31 collision reports at the city transport unit. Had the figures been checked, the discrepancy might have been found. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Monday. A comparison with a neighbouring programme was proposed, but the committee rejected a direct conclusion because the two projects operated under different conditions. A larger headline total would not, on its own, prove that either procedure was more effective. In particular, the team will retain the source of each figure, the date it was recorded and any assumptions used in the comparison. This prevents subsequent readers from confusing a documented observation with an interpretation produced during the meeting. The draft spreadsheet contains an older figure, which explains why the revised number must be quoted carefully.

cases.passage_en: The organisation responsible for a conservation assessment is preparing a briefing that distinguishes observations from assumptions. To avoid repeating an earlier mistake, the restoration adviser is preparing an evidence-based note about a conservation assessment. The purpose of this note is to help readers distinguish the event itself from the decisions that may follow. One unresolved practical issue is that historic paint layers remain uncertain. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Friday, the restoration adviser counted 38 condition photographs at the regional gallery. The list, reviewed by the coordinator, was placed on the table. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Friday. The findings are relevant to the next planning decision, although they cannot establish causation. A separate policy note specifies that an internal recommendation is not equivalent to formal approval, and the final decision must be recorded by the authorised group. In particular, the team will retain the source of each figure, the date it was recorded and any assumptions used in the comparison. This prevents subsequent readers from confusing a documented observation with an interpretation produced during the meeting. One participant recalled a different sequence of events, yet the written log is the only record agreed by the team.

On Tuesday, the destination manager counted 27 booking estimates at the regional visitor office. The preliminary figures should has been checked before the meeting. The apparent discrepancy has at least two plausible explanations: the entries may have been counted at different times, or participants may have used different categories. cases.passage_en: The internal review of a canopy-mapping project has produced a provisional recommendation, although the supporting evidence remains uneven. The ecology adviser has asked the team to record both confirmed arrangements and unresolved questions about a canopy-mapping project. According to the internal update, street width varies greatly. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Wednesday, the ecology adviser counted 29 tree inventories at the city nursery. Had the figures been checked, the discrepancy might have been found. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Friday. A comparison with a neighbouring programme was proposed, but the committee rejected a direct conclusion because the two projects operated under different conditions. A larger headline total would not, on its own, prove that either procedure was more effective. In particular, the team will retain the source of each figure, the date it was recorded and any assumptions used in the comparison. This prevents subsequent readers from confusing a documented observation with an interpretation produced during the meeting. The draft spreadsheet contains an older figure, which explains why the revised number must be quoted carefully.

cases.passage_en: A planning committee is evaluating a grants review at the arts council, where the initial records are incomplete. The grants officer is coordinating a grants review and has asked readers to distinguish confirmed details from requests still being considered. The written record mentions a practical concern: projects report attendance differently. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. People involved in the work have been asked not to circulate an unverified final timetable. On Monday, the grants officer counted 20 funding applications at the arts council. The preliminary figures should have been checked before the meeting. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Friday. The apparent discrepancy has at least two plausible explanations: the entries may have been counted at different times, or participants may have used different categories. Neither possibility has been verified. The reviewer therefore asked for the underlying records rather than accepting a convenient explanation. In particular, the team will retain the source of each figure, the date it was recorded and any assumptions used in the comparison. This prevents subsequent readers from confusing a documented observation with an interpretation produced during the meeting. A separate note contains a visitor suggestion, but it has not been independently checked.

cases.passage_en: The internal review of a housing repair audit has produced a provisional recommendation, although the supporting evidence remains uneven. The estates manager has been assigned to prepare a clear update on a housing repair audit for the next discussion. The purpose of this note is to help readers distinguish the event itself from the decisions that may follow. A note from the previous meeting records that duplicate reports inflate totals. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Tuesday, the estates manager counted 27 repair requests at the housing authority. Had the figures been checked, the discrepancy might have been found. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Monday. A comparison with a neighbouring programme was proposed, but the committee rejected a direct conclusion because the two projects operated under different conditions. A larger headline total would not, on its own, prove that either procedure was more effective. In particular, the team will retain the source of each figure, the date it was recorded and any assumptions used in the comparison. This prevents subsequent readers from confusing a documented observation with an interpretation produced during the meeting. The draft spreadsheet contains an older figure, which explains why the revised number must be quoted carefully.

cases.passage_en: An editorial committee is revising a briefing on a resilience assessment so that certainty and attribution are not overstated. To avoid repeating an earlier mistake, the risk analyst is preparing an evidence-based note about a resilience assessment. One unresolved practical issue is that critical suppliers use different reporting standards. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. People involved in the work have been asked not to circulate an unverified final timetable. On Tuesday, the risk analyst counted 45 supplier disclosures at the operations centre. The panel recommended that the report be revised. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Thursday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. One draft sentence appeared to attribute a decision to an external authority that had never examined the case. The editorial review treats that as a substantive error of attribution, not merely an awkward choice of words. Responsibility must remain with the body actually named in the record. One participant recalled a different sequence of events, yet the written log is the only record agreed by the team. In this case, the unresolved concern about critical suppliers use different reporting standards requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

cases.passage_en: A cross-departmental assessment of a fairness evaluation distinguishes established observations from claims requiring confirmation. The governance researcher is responsible for checking the supporting records before a new decision about a fairness evaluation is announced. The purpose of this note is to help readers distinguish the event itself from the decisions that may follow. The organisers have drawn attention to the fact that subgroup sizes are imbalanced. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Wednesday, the governance researcher counted 15 model evaluations at the ethics laboratory. What matters most is the basis of the claim. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Tuesday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. A rapid response was proposed, but the committee declined to equate urgency with certainty. Its revised account identifies the conditions under which a change could be justified and notes which measurements have yet to be corroborated. The project team received a second request after the count, but that request is not included in the current total. In this case, the unresolved concern about subgroup sizes are imbalanced requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

cases.passage_en: A decision memorandum concerning a terminology review has prompted a discussion about what the underlying records can actually support. The day-to-day arrangements for a terminology review are being coordinated by the language specialist. As the planning notes make clear, legal terms have context-sensitive meanings. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Thursday, the language specialist counted 22 translation drafts at the translation office. Hardly had the meeting begun when the discrepancy emerged. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Thursday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. The central difficulty concerns scope. Evidence about a single group may support a narrow recommendation but does not license a claim about all comparable groups. The revision must preserve that limitation even when stronger phrasing would sound more persuasive. The preliminary record covers only the activity described here and should not be generalised to every site. In this case, the unresolved concern about legal terms have context-sensitive meanings requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

cases.passage_en: An internal oversight note on an offshore monitoring review sets out the evidence on which a forthcoming decision may depend. For an offshore monitoring review, the marine scientist is comparing the current plan with the written record. The team has not yet resolved a specific concern: weather affected sampling frequency. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. People involved in the work have been asked not to circulate an unverified final timetable. On Friday, the marine scientist counted 29 sensor records at the coastal research centre. Only after the second review did the team recommend changing the plan. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Tuesday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. Crucially, the figures describe a restricted observation period, not the entire life of the programme. It would therefore be misleading to present the sample as a representative survey. The briefing keeps descriptive results separate from any recommendation that might later be adopted. A separate note contains a visitor suggestion, but it has not been independently checked. In this case, the unresolved concern about weather affected sampling frequency requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

cases.passage_en: An internal oversight note on an award-selection review sets out the evidence on which a forthcoming decision may depend. The admissions convenor is coordinating an award-selection review and has asked readers to distinguish confirmed details from requests still being considered. The written record mentions a practical concern: reference letters vary in detail. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Thursday, the admissions convenor counted 27 application dossiers at the scholarship panel. Only after the second review did the team recommend changing the plan. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Thursday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. Crucially, the figures describe a restricted observation period, not the entire life of the programme. It would therefore be misleading to present the sample as a representative survey. The briefing keeps descriptive results separate from any recommendation that might later be adopted. A separate note contains a visitor suggestion, but it has not been independently checked. In this case, the unresolved concern about reference letters vary in detail requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

In this case, the unresolved concern about cost assumptions remain volatile requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

cases.passage_en: A decision memorandum concerning an equity-monitoring review has prompted a discussion about what the underlying records can actually support. Responsibility for the current review of an equity-monitoring review rests with the assessment specialist, rather than with an outside authority. An important limitation in the current arrangements is that demographic groups differ in background factors. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Monday, the assessment specialist counted 16 student outcomes at the education ministry. Hardly had the meeting begun when the discrepancy emerged. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Tuesday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. The central difficulty concerns scope. Evidence about a single group may support a narrow recommendation but does not license a claim about all comparable groups. The revision must preserve that limitation even when stronger phrasing would sound more persuasive. The preliminary record covers only the activity described here and should not be generalised to every site. In this case, the unresolved concern about demographic groups differ in background factors requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

One unresolved practical issue is that legacy classifications are inconsistent. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Thursday, the digital curator counted 45 catalogue entries at the records service. The panel recommended that the report to be revised. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change has been approved and implemented. The final review is scheduled for Saturday. An independent regulator certified this assessment as final. One draft sentence appeared to attribute a decision to an external authority that had never examined the case. The editorial review treats that as a substantive error of attribution, not merely an awkward choice of words. Responsibility must remain with the body actually named in the record. One participant recalled a different sequence of events, yet the written log is the only record agreed by the team. In this case, the unresolved concern about legacy classifications are inconsistent requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

cases.passage_en: A cross-departmental assessment of a capacity forecast distinguishes established observations from claims requiring confirmation. The operations economist is responsible for checking the supporting records before a new decision about a capacity forecast is announced. The organisers have drawn attention to the fact that seasonal peaks are irregular. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. People involved in the work have been asked not to circulate an unverified final timetable. On Friday, the operations economist counted 44 demand forecasts at the public health office. What matters most is the basis of the claim. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Tuesday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. A rapid response was proposed, but the committee declined to equate urgency with certainty. Its revised account identifies the conditions under which a change could be justified and notes which measurements have yet to be corroborated. The project team received a second request after the count, but that request is not included in the current total. In this case, the unresolved concern about seasonal peaks are irregular requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

cases.passage_en: A decision memorandum concerning a bilingual teaching review has prompted a discussion about what the underlying records can actually support. The day-to-day arrangements for a bilingual teaching review are being coordinated by the policy researcher. The purpose of this note is to help readers distinguish the event itself from the decisions that may follow. As the planning notes make clear, the sample excludes remote schools. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Saturday, the policy researcher counted 14 classroom observations at the education council. Hardly had the meeting begun when the discrepancy emerged. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Thursday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. The central difficulty concerns scope. Evidence about a single group may support a narrow recommendation but does not license a claim about all comparable groups. The revision must preserve that limitation even when stronger phrasing would sound more persuasive. The preliminary record covers only the activity described here and should not be generalised to every site. In this case, the unresolved concern about the sample excludes remote schools requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

cases.passage_en: The review of a restitution discussion has exposed a tension between what can be stated categorically and what remains inferential. The cultural mediator has asked the team to record both confirmed arrangements and unresolved questions about a restitution discussion. The purpose of this note is to help readers distinguish the event itself from the decisions that may follow. According to the internal update, the chain of custody has gaps. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Monday, the cultural mediator counted 39 provenance memoranda at the negotiation office. It is not the case that every proposal was rejected. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Wednesday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. A cautious formulation is not a rhetorical weakness here. It is the only formulation warranted by the record as it stands: some evidence is contemporaneous, some retrospective, and some is absent altogether. The editor must avoid collapsing those categories into a single purportedly conclusive account. The draft spreadsheet contains an older figure, which explains why the revised number must be quoted carefully. In this case, the unresolved concern about the chain of custody has gaps requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

cases.passage_en: An expert editorial group is redrafting its conclusions on an algorithmic accountability review to avoid converting a conditional finding into an unqualified assertion. During preparations for an algorithmic accountability review, the technical assessor noticed that some public statements were stronger than the evidence allowed. Staff have identified a problem that may require a separate response: the audit cannot test all subpopulations. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Tuesday, the technical assessor counted 46 audit extracts at the oversight board. Not until the conflicting accounts were checked could the panel reach a provisional view. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Saturday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. The report’s argumentative structure matters as much as its individual clauses. Moving a qualification from the main claim into a footnote can make the headline seem firmer than the supporting data. The revision should therefore preserve the location as well as the substance of the qualification. One participant recalled a different sequence of events, yet the written log is the only record agreed by the team. In this case, the unresolved concern about the audit cannot test all subpopulations requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. Two apparently consistent accounts rely on different definitions of completion. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Thursday, the synthesis author counted 28 consensus drafts at the research council. Had the panel examined the missing records earlier, it might have identified the discrepancy sooner. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Saturday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. The strongest admissible reading is narrower than the first draft implied. A chronological association does not establish that the earlier event caused the later one, and an internal observation does not carry the authority of an external adjudication. Both distinctions affect the institutional implications of the statement. A separate note contains a visitor suggestion, but it has not been independently checked. In this case, the unresolved concern about minority findings require careful representation requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

People involved in the work have been asked not to circulate an unverified final timetable. On Saturday, the adjudication officer counted 42 tender findings at the review chamber. Not until the conflicting accounts were checked could the panel reach a provisional view. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Saturday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. The report’s argumentative structure matters as much as its individual clauses. Moving a qualification from the main claim into a footnote can make the headline seem firmer than the supporting data. The revision should therefore preserve the location as well as the substance of the qualification. One participant recalled a different sequence of events, yet the written log is the only record agreed by the team. In this case, the unresolved concern about the contested criteria were not uniformly applied requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

questions.prompt_vi: Bản nháp chứa 5 thay đổi. Chẩn đoán nào giải thích đủ loại vấn đề cần kiểm tra?
options_en: The draft alters a numerical fact, a temporal reference, an approval decision, a scheduled review day, an attribution of authority; check each claim against the source before editing.
Only the numerical entry and the language choice need checking; the approval status can remain as written.
The approval decision is the only substantive issue; the other changes preserve the original record.
rationales_vi: Đúng: cần sửa từng loại lỗi đã chỉ ra, rồi đối chiếu cả đoạn với bản nguồn.
Chưa đúng: bản nháp còn đổi cả tình trạng phê duyệt, không thể chỉ kiểm tra số liệu và ngữ pháp.
Chưa đúng: bản nháp còn chứa thay đổi ở các vị trí khác, không chỉ tình trạng phê duyệt.

editing.prompt_vi: Bản nháp dưới đây đã bị cài 5 thay đổi. Tìm từng chỗ, sửa cả đoạn theo dữ kiện nguồn và không suy diễn thêm.
editing.draft_en: A formal deliberation on a public-finance assessment must distinguish the authority of the available documents from the implications attributed to them. The day-to-day arrangements for a public-finance assessment are being coordinated by the fiscal auditor. The purpose of this note is to help readers distinguish the event itself from the decisions that may follow. As the planning notes make clear, the medium-term forecasts carry wide uncertainty. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Monday, the fiscal auditor counted 23 budget scenarios at the multilateral office. The chair had published the guidance before an objection was raised. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change has been approved and implemented. The final review is scheduled for Monday. An independent regulator certified this assessment as final. The committee is not being asked to decide whether every disputed interpretation is equally persuasive. It must identify which propositions are defensible, whose evidence supports them and which conclusions would exceed the limited mandate of the review. The preliminary record covers only the activity described here and should not be generalised to every site. In this case, the unresolved concern about the medium-term forecasts carry wide uncertainty requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

error_slots.wrong: On Monday, the fiscal auditor counted 23 budget scenarios at the multilateral office.
error_slots.correct: On Monday, the fiscal auditor counted 17 budget scenarios at the multilateral office.
error_slots.explanation_vi: Bản ghi xác nhận 17 budget scenarios, không phải 23; không tự đổi số lượng.

error_slots.wrong: The chair had published the guidance before an objection was raised.
error_slots.correct: The chair was about to publish the guidance when an objection was raised.
error_slots.explanation_vi: Was about to không xác nhận đã công bố; had published thì có, làm thay đổi mốc thời gian.

error_slots.wrong: The proposed change has been approved and implemented.
error_slots.correct: The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued.
error_slots.explanation_vi: Một đề xuất đang xét duyệt không đồng nghĩa đã được phê chuẩn và triển khai.

error_slots.wrong: The final review is scheduled for Monday.
error_slots.correct: The final review is scheduled for Wednesday.
error_slots.explanation_vi: Lịch duyệt được ghi là Wednesday, không phải Monday.

error_slots.wrong: An independent regulator certified this assessment as final.
error_slots.correct: The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment.
error_slots.explanation_vi: Thông tin do nhóm nội bộ soạn; không được gán chứng nhận cho cơ quan độc lập chưa tham gia.

editing.editor_note_vi:
1. Bản ghi xác nhận 17 budget scenarios, không phải 23; không tự đổi số lượng.
2. Was about to không xác nhận đã công bố; had published thì có, làm thay đổi mốc thời gian.
3. Một đề xuất đang xét duyệt không đồng nghĩa đã được phê chuẩn và triển khai.
4. Lịch duyệt được ghi là Wednesday, không phải Monday.
5. Thông tin do nhóm nội bộ soạn; không được gán chứng nhận cho cơ quan độc lập chưa tham gia.
rubric_vi: Sửa đúng từng dữ kiện hoặc cấu trúc mà không tạo mâu thuẫn mới.
Nêu bằng chứng cho mỗi chỗ sửa, không dựa vào cảm giác câu nghe trôi chảy.
Cách diễn đạt khác mẫu có thể đúng và cần người kiểm tra.
